tools.name: get_agent_session
tools.description: Retrieve a Replo session's current status, latest response, tool activity, errors, and pending interactions (permission requests and questions). Use to check progress after starting or continuing a session. When pendingInteractions is non-empty, show it to the user and wait for their answer, then pass it to resolve_agent_interaction: a choice takes one option value as the decision; a form takes one answers array per step. For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

tools.name: resolve_agent_interaction
tools.description: Resolve one pending Replo agent interaction with the user's explicit answer. For a permission request, pass type permission and the decision from its response options. For a question, pass type question and one answers array per form step, in order, holding the selected option values, or the user's own text only where that step's allowCustom is true; an empty array skips a step. Never infer an answer. Approving or answering resumes the agent, which can then overwrite or delete content, publish, or write to an external service. Returns the updated session status; an interaction that is no longer pending returns an error and nothing is delivered, so call get_agent_session again. For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

interactionId.description: The id copied from get_agent_session.pendingInteractions after the user answers using that interaction's response contract.

decision.description: For a permission: the user's selected option value from its response contract.

answers.description: For a question: one array per form step, in order.

tools.name: abort_agent_session
tools.description: Cancel the in-progress turn of a Replo session. Cancellation interrupts unfinished work and may leave partial changes. Completed changes are not rolled back, and the session is retained. For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

tools.name: query_replo_analytics
tools.description: Run read-only ClickHouse SQL over a project's Replo analytics for traffic, conversion, revenue, and session-level questions. No saved Insights report is required. Use this for ad hoc questions or when list_insights_reports finds no relevant report; an empty report list does not mean analytics are unavailable. Only SELECT/WITH queries are accepted, and project-scoped tables are automatically restricted to the requested project and its authorized same-workspace, same-store siblings. Table columns and external metric views are listed in the query input schema. Also supports connected external metrics through those parameterized views. Check get_integration_status before querying; external data can be cached for eight hours and an empty result does not prove zero activity. Use provider tools for discovery or provider-native reports. Before writing a query, read the querying-analytics skill (call skills with name "querying-analytics").

query.description:
Run a read-only analytics query for a project.

Rules:
- Use SELECT or WITH queries only.
- Do not add project or namespace filters; project scoping is enforced server-side.
- Use session_attribution(since, until) for cross-project session and attributed revenue; stored computed metrics and page rollups are project-local.
- Session revenue repeats across visited pages: deduplicate by subject for totals. Attributed revenue splits credit across eligible pageviews before domain filters.
- Aggregate-state rollup columns must use the matching ClickHouse merge function, such as countMerge, uniqMerge, or sumMerge, and queries must group by selected dimensions.
- Maximum execution time: 60 seconds.
- Maximum result rows: 100000.

Queryable tables, their columns, and the external metric views for connected integrations are listed at https://docs.replo.app/api-reference/analytics-tables.

External metric views take named since/until dates (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive); the views that also need settings JSON or another argument say so on that page. Credentials and project scope are injected server-side: never supply auth_token or project_id.
In MCP, call get_integration_status first for connection IDs, setup links, and supported views. Missing or misconfigured integrations can return zero rows: do not report that as measured zero activity. Use provider-specific tools for metric/property discovery and detailed provider-native reports.
External results can be cached for up to eight hours, and report views cap provider results at 10,000 rows; narrow dates or dimensions if exceeded. Match currencies, reporting timezones, and attribution definitions before combining sources.

Queryable tables, as name(columns), project scoped unless marked:
- session_attribution(subject UUID, date DateTime64(3), name LowCardinality(String), domain String, path String, title String, purchaseRevenueUsd Float64, sessionRevenueUsd Float64, sessionPurchaseCount UInt64, attributedRevenueUsd Float64): Parameterized view: session_attribution(since='YYYY-MM-DD', until='YYYY-MM-DD'), inclusive UTC dates. Computes USD purchase, session, and equal-pageview attributed revenue across authorized sibling projects within that window, before domain filters. Cart/checkout views receive no attribution. Deduplicate sessionRevenueUsd by subject before summing. Inherits source row policies.
- events_computed(subject UUID, date DateTime64(3), name LowCardinality(String), path String, domain String, currencyCode String, subjectPurchaseSum Float64, subjectPurchaseCount Float64, subjectPurchaseFraction Float64, subjectPurchaseFractionalSum Float64, title String): Raw events with project-local computed session metrics. Use session_attribution for revenue across linked projects.
- currency_exchange_rates(date Date, code String, rate Float32): Currency exchange rates for multi-currency reporting. Not project scoped.
- daily_page_rollups(day Date, domain String, path String, utm_source String, views_state AggregateFunction(count), unique_sessions_state AggregateFunction(uniq, UUID), converting_sessions_state AggregateFunction(uniq, UUID), fractional_conversions_state AggregateFunction(sum, Float64), fractional_revenue_usd_state AggregateFunction(sum, Float64), session_conversions_state AggregateFunction(sum, UInt64), session_revenue_usd_state AggregateFunction(sum, Float64)): Pre-aggregated daily page metrics by day, domain, path, and UTM source. Revenue/conversion attribution is project-local; use session_attribution across linked projects.
- daily_namespace_rollups(day Date, utm_source String, views_state AggregateFunction(count), unique_sessions_state AggregateFunction(uniq, UUID), converting_sessions_state AggregateFunction(uniq, UUID)): Pre-aggregated daily project traffic metrics by day and UTM source.
- daily_namespace_purchase_rollups(day Date, utm_source String, purchase_count_state AggregateFunction(count), total_revenue_usd_state AggregateFunction(sum, Float64), unique_purchasing_sessions_state AggregateFunction(uniq, UUID)): Pre-aggregated daily purchase metrics by day and UTM source.
- benchmark_comparison(date Date, peers_date Date, metric String, window_days UInt16, days_covered UInt16, suspected_bot_sessions UInt64, channel String, device String, my_value Nullable(Float64), peer_blended Nullable(Float64), peer_p25 Nullable(Float64), peer_median Nullable(Float64), peer_p75 Nullable(Float64), peer_p90 Nullable(Float64), peer_brands UInt32, confidence String, compared_category String, compared_location String, compared_price_tier String, comparison_level String, my_price_tier String, my_aov_90d_usd Float64, my_location String): Parameterized view: benchmark_comparison(window_days=1|7|30|90, since='YYYY-MM-DD', until='YYYY-MM-DD', channel='all'|'affiliate'|'email_sms'|'ai_assistant'|'paid_social'|'paid_search'|'organic_social'|'other_tagged'|'organic_search'|'direct'|'referral', device='all'|'mobile'|'tablet'|'desktop', by_location=0|1, by_price_tier=0|1). One row per day and metric: this project's own value over the window next to anonymized peers in the deepest cohort that passes (10+ brands, not low confidence). It keeps the asked-for axes and the narrowest category it can, trying country, then sub-region, then region at each category level, then drops price tier, then location. Price tiers are p0_25, p25_50, p50_75, p75_100: quartiles of peer brands' 90-day AOV in the root category; a brand with under 30 orders in 90 days has none. A brand in the top 10% or top 1% is compared within p90_100 or p99_100 when that band has enough brands. Metrics: sessions, pages_per_session, add_to_cart_rate, checkout_rate, conversion_rate, orders, revenue_usd, aov_usd, revenue_per_session_usd, and, only when channel='all' and device='all', the traffic shares channel_share_<channel> (one per channel above) and device_share_<device> (mobile, tablet, desktop): the share of this brand's sessions from that channel or device, next to peers' own shares, where a peer with none counts as 0. They need no checkout data. A brand with no category and no orders is compared on sessions, pages_per_session and the shares with all brands in every vertical (comparison_level 'all brands'), and on nothing else. days_covered is how many of the window's days have data: fewer than window_days means history is shorter than the window or the project had no sessions on some days. suspected_bot_sessions is how many sessions were taken out of my_value as suspected bot traffic (a channel and device with 3 times its usual sessions that view one page and don't add to cart or buy); peers are cleaned the same way, and Insights still counts these sessions. Peer columns are NULL when no cohort passes. Inherits source row policies.
- benchmark_trend(date Date, metric String, my_value Nullable(Float64), peer_blended Nullable(Float64), peer_median Nullable(Float64), peer_p25 Nullable(Float64), peer_p75 Nullable(Float64), peer_brands UInt32, compared_category String, my_sma Nullable(Float64), peer_sma Nullable(Float64), my_ema Nullable(Float64), peer_ema Nullable(Float64)): Parameterized view: benchmark_trend(since, until, channel, device, by_location, by_price_tier, ma_days, ema_days). benchmark_comparison over 1-day windows plus moving averages per metric: my_sma and peer_sma over the last ma_days days, my_ema and peer_ema with an ema_days half-life. Days without a value are skipped, not counted as 0. Inherits source row policies.
- daily_category_benchmarks(snapshot_date Date, window_days UInt16, vertical LowCardinality(String), category_level UInt8, category_key String, channel LowCardinality(String), device LowCardinality(String), location_level UInt8, location_key String, price_tier LowCardinality(String), metric LowCardinality(String), brands UInt32, blended Float64, p25 Float64, p50 Float64, p75 Float64, p90 Nullable(Float64), mean Float64, stddev Float64, rse Float64, confidence LowCardinality(String)): Anonymized daily peer statistics per cohort, readable across projects. One row per snapshot_date, window_days (1, 7, 30, 90), vertical (ecommerce, saas, services, or all: every vertical together, traffic metrics only, with no categories or price tiers), category_key (an industry path such as 'Home & Garden > Kitchen & Dining', or '' for the whole vertical), channel, device (mobile, tablet, desktop), location_key (the brand's home location (location path such as '/Europe/Western Europe/Germany', or '' for everywhere), price_tier (p0_25, p25_50, p50_75, p75_100, plus the overlapping top bands p90_100 and p99_100) and metric; 'all' (or '') on an axis means not cut by it. blended is pooled across brands and one large brand can move it; p25 to p90 are brand-level quantiles. Rows need 10 brands. Traffic shares (channel_share_<channel>, device_share_<device>) are on channel='all', device='all' rows only. confidence is high, medium or low from the relative standard error, or for shares from the standard error in share points: never show low rows to customers. Query with FINAL. Not project scoped.
- daily_namespace_benchmark_profiles(snapshot_date Date, brand String, vertical LowCardinality(String), category_path Array(String), country_code LowCardinality(String), location_path Array(String), aov_90d_usd Float64, orders_90d UInt64, price_tier LowCardinality(String), top_bands Array(String), tier_p25_usd Nullable(Float64), tier_p50_usd Nullable(Float64), tier_p75_usd Nullable(Float64), tier_p90_usd Nullable(Float64), tier_p99_usd Nullable(Float64)): This project's brand (root domain) and its value on every benchmark axis per day: vertical, category_path, location_path, 90-day AOV and orders (its own, with the projects in its workspace on the same Shopify store, never another workspace's project on the same domain), price tier, top bands (p90_100, p99_100) it's in, and its root category's tier boundaries (tier_p25_usd to tier_p99_usd, NULL until the category has enough priced peers). Query with FINAL.
- benchmark_brand_metrics(as_of Date, window_days UInt16, days_covered UInt16, brand String, channel String, device String, sessions UInt64, page_views UInt64, add_to_cart_sessions UInt64, checkout_sessions UInt64, purchase_sessions UInt64, orders UInt64, revenue_usd Float64, suspected_bot_sessions UInt64): Parameterized view: benchmark_brand_metrics(start='YYYY-MM-DD', end='YYYY-MM-DD'). This project's brand totals per as_of day, 1/7/30/90-day window, channel and device ('all' included on both), as used for its benchmarks. days_covered is how many of the window's days have data. Suspected bot traffic is taken out of sessions and page_views, and suspected_bot_sessions counts it. Prefer benchmark_comparison. Inherits source row policies.
- daily_namespace_benchmark_rollups(day Date, channel LowCardinality(String), device LowCardinality(String), sessions UInt64, page_views UInt64, add_to_cart_sessions UInt64, checkout_sessions UInt64, purchase_sessions UInt64, orders UInt64, revenue_usd Float64): This project's daily benchmark inputs by session channel and device, built from each session 3 hours after it starts (bots excluded). Each session is on exactly one row, so sum() the counts across rows and days. revenue_usd is converted at the purchase day's rate.
- benchmark_namespace_domain(root_domain String, views_30d UInt64, updated_at DateTime): The root domain this project is benchmarked as: the one its pages got the most views on in the last 30 days. Query with FINAL.

External metric views: triplewhale_metrics_daily, triplewhale_metrics_totals, triplewhale_metrics_list, contentsquare_metrics_daily, contentsquare_metrics_totals, contentsquare_metrics_list, mixpanel_metrics_daily, mixpanel_metrics_totals, mixpanel_metrics_list, lifetimely_metrics_daily, lifetimely_metrics_totals, lifetimely_metrics_list, faire_metrics_daily, faire_metrics_totals, faire_metrics_list, alia_metrics_daily, alia_metrics_totals, alia_metrics_list, intelligems_metrics_daily, intelligems_metrics_totals, intelligems_metrics_list, intelligems_experience_metrics_daily, intelligems_experience_metrics_totals, intelligems_experience_metrics_list, meta_ads_ad_daily, meta_ads_campaign_daily, replo_roi_monthly, shopify_sales_monthly, google_analytics_report, google_search_console_report.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: Find the Replo site to inspect, manage, or clone within a project. Each site returns clone_url, the URL used to clone that site's code over Git, and is_default. When the user does not name a site, use the site with is_default true; if no site is default, ask which one to use. Results are paginated: follow next_cursor until has_more is false before concluding a site does not exist. Site names are dashboard labels, not SEO page titles. Before cloning, pulling or pushing a site's code, read the local-development skill (call skills with name "local-development").

tools.name: create_site
tools.description: Create a site in a Replo project together with its git repository, forked from a published starter template ('blank' unless template is given). Pass projectId from list_projects and a name for the site. Returns the site with clone_url; clone it over Git with a repo key from create_api_key. Creation usually takes seconds; if it takes longer, the result is { id, status: 'creating' } instead: the site is still being created, so call list_sites shortly to get it rather than creating it again. Creating a site does not publish it. Before creating or editing a site or page, read the building-sites skill (call skills with name "building-sites").

name.description: Dashboard display name for the new site.

template.description: Published starter template to fork the site's repository from, e.g. 'notion'. Defaults to 'blank'.

tools.name: update_site
tools.description: Rename a Replo site's dashboard display name. This does not change its SEO page title, which lives in the site's layout metadata, or its published page content. Use list_sites to find site IDs. For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

siteId.description: The ID of the site to rename. Use list_sites to find site IDs.

name.description: The new human-readable display name for the site. This is the site's name shown in the dashboard, distinct from the SEO page title in the site's layout metadata.

tools.name: publish_site
tools.description: Publish a site to make changes live. Requires the siteId from list_sites. Builds, packages, uploads, and deploys. Before publishing, read the publishing-sites skill (call skills with name "publishing-sites").

siteId.description: The ID of the site to publish. Get this from list_sites. The tool finds the site's folder on disk itself, so there is nothing else to look up.

promoteRoutes.description: Routes whose unpublished edits go live in this publish — pages and content entries alike, e.g. ["/", "/about", "/blog/my-post"] (a content entry's route is /<collection>/<slug>). Omit to publish every page and entry with changes. Pass [] to publish only site-wide changes and leave every page and entry draft as it is.

tools.name: apply_branding_to_site
tools.description: Apply the project's saved brand to the selected site's shared style tokens, fonts, layout, and shared components. Affects that site's drafts, not the saved brand kit. Use update_brand first if there is no saved brand. Starts an asynchronous internal-agent operation; poll get_agent_session. For corrections, call this same tool with its sessionId and unchanged target. Requires a provisioned site. Source edits may execute in its preview. The Replo agent uses its normal tools and connected integrations to implement and verify the requested changes. Use publish_site separately to make changes public. Before restyling a site with a brand, read the managing-brand skill (call skills with name "managing-brand").

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: List a project's Replo automations (scheduled tasks). For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: Inspect the schedule and current timing of a specific Replo automation (scheduled task). For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

taskId.description: ID of the scheduled task to inspect.

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Schedule a Replo automation: a prompt Replo's agent runs later for the project, once or on a recurrence (rrule). It does not run now. Each run happens without the user, so the prompt must be self-contained, and you should confirm the prompt, first run time and timezone with the user before calling. Give scheduledAt as a future ISO time with the user's timezone offset. To email each run's results, set delivery recipients. Check list_tasks first so you don't create a duplicate. For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

title.description: Short human-readable title for the task.

emoji.description: Emoji label used to visually group this task in the schedule UI.

prompt.description: The exact prompt the task should run. This must be self-contained and executable without asking the user follow-up questions. Include any reasonable assumptions needed to complete the task, and do not include instructions like 'ask the user' or 'wait for clarification'.

scheduledAt.description: ISO 8601 date-time with an explicit timezone offset when the task should first run. Must be in the future.

rrule.description: RRULE string for recurrence, such as FREQ=DAILY. Use FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=1 for one-time tasks.

delivery.description: Where each run's results go, e.g. { email: { recipients: ["me@brand.com"] } }. When the user wants results delivered, default to their own address. `{ email: { recipients: [] } }` turns email off; omitting it on update keeps the current delivery.

playbookId.description: Id of the playbook this task is based on, when the user picked one; its sample email becomes the run's layout guideline.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Change a Replo automation (scheduled task). Read it with get_task first: title, prompt and rrule are always replaced, so pass the current values for any the user isn't changing, and pass the current emoji too or it resets to ✨; omitting delivery keeps it. Pass scheduledAt, a future ISO time with the user's timezone offset, for the next run: without it the schedule restarts from now, which moves the time of day and leaves a one-time automation with no run. Confirm the change with the user before calling. For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

tools.name: delete_task
tools.description: Permanently delete a Replo automation (scheduled task) and stop all future runs. Use this when the user no longer wants a scheduled prompt to run. For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

taskId.description: ID of the scheduled task to delete.

tools.name: get_integration_status
tools.description: Check one integration's connection status in the selected Replo project. Returns connected, not_connected, or needs_reconnect. needs_reconnect means every connection is stale; a connection's own needsReconnect flag marks a stale one when others are not. For an integration the user connects, connectUrl is the link to give them: Replo signs them in, then they connect it to the project in one click; when they say they're done, call this again to confirm it's connected. externalAnalytics lists supported SQL views and their maximum cache age, not proof the connection can fetch metrics. Check this before querying external metrics, including when a provider's tools are absent from your catalog. Analytics integration keys include triple-whale, contentsquare, intelligems, meta-marketing-api, google-analytics, google-search-console, shopify, and converge. connectFailureMessage explains a failed connection attempt. isAlwaysAvailable identifies a built-in integration; isSettingsManaged identifies setup in integration settings. This tool does not connect an account or change permissions. Each integration has a skill named by its key: before using an integration's tools, read it (call skills with name "shopify", for example).

projectId.description: Replo project id, from list_projects.

tools.name: get_branding
tools.description: Read the live brand: version, facts, the business and design overviews (markdown), colors with roles (hex is authoritative), fonts, marks, personas, tagged context files, the Brand Studio imagery (the merchant's own photos, the first choice for page images), and the brand's imported Figma designs. Version 0 with empty fields means no brand yet. `extraction` is the latest website import: poll this with increasing delays until its importId matches the one update_brand returned and its status is completed or failed. Read-only. Read the brand's files by id with read_file; the paths are where Replo's agent reads them. Does not start an agent session. Before creating or changing a brand kit, read the managing-brand skill (call skills with name "managing-brand").

projectId.description: The project whose saved brand to read.

tools.name: update_brand
tools.description: Create or update the saved brand kit, with `ops` or from a public site's `url`. Never applies branding to an existing site or publishes it. `ops`: business facts, the business and design overviews, colors, fonts, personas, logo marks, and which Drive files count as brand context; brand ops apply in order in one transaction, file ops run after it. `url`: Replo reads the site into the brand on its servers by `mode`: replace (default, whole brand) · swap (only `parts`, in full) · fill (keep what's set, fill gaps); a figma.com file link instead adds the file to the brand's Figma designs. Statuses: applied (saved at the returned version) · partial (brand saved, a file op refused; see files) · invalid (what was refused; nothing was written) · running (an import started and returns at once with `importId`: poll get_branding until it is completed or failed, under extraction for a site or figmaDesigns for a Figma file) · failed (the import could not start; see message) · action_required (the person must act first, such as connecting Figma; see connectUrl and message). A null value deletes that item, and a replace overwrites what was there. An import returns at once with an importId; follow it with get_branding instead of calling this again. A project gets 50 calls with a url a day, whether or not they start an import; ops don't count. Does not start an agent session. Before creating or changing a brand kit, read the managing-brand skill (call skills with name "managing-brand").

ops.description: Ops in order; fill only the fields your op uses. setColor value: { key, name, hex: "#rrggbb", category: "brand" | "neutral", roles: string[], usage: string | null, position: integer }. setFont value: { key, family, roles: string[], delivery: "google-fonts" | "cdn" | "uploaded" | "system" | "unknown", license: string | null, usage: string | null, position: integer, faces: [{ weight: 1-1000, style: "normal" | "italic", assetId: uuid | null, sourceUrl: string | null }] }. setBusiness patch: any of name, about, audience, pricePoint, businessModel, foundedYear, location, voice, sourceUrl. setOverview: kind "business" | "design" and markdown. setMarks: logoAssetId, faviconAssetId or logomarkAssetId; upload the image with upload_asset first and pass the asset id it returns. setPersona value: copy a persona from get_branding and change what you need; a persona nickname is a segment label, never a person's name. A refused op comes back with `expected`, the exact shape to resend. Pass ops or url, not both.

patch.description: setBusiness: the business fields to change.

markdown.description: setOverview: the whole overview as markdown; null clears it.

key.description: setColor, setFont, setPersona: the item's key.

tools.name: create_artifact

Send files keyed by path: index.html is the page, each *.insights.json is an Insights report, and report.insights.json is the main report (Replo renders the page around it when index.html is omitted). Add CSS, scripts, data and images alongside. Saves to My Files unless parentId names another folder. Returns the artifact folder ID and its viewer link; then call show_artifact with the folder ID so the user sees it. Creation is private; call set_file_sharing with the folder ID only when the user asks to share it. For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

Each *.insights.json file is an Insights report document (version "2.0", the shape get_insights_report returns) whose saved queries run live for each viewer; embed one with <replo-report src="./sales.insights.json"></replo-report>. report.insights.json is the artifact's main report, the one the Insights report tools read, and without index.html Replo renders the page around it.

tools.name: update_artifact
tools.description: Replace parts of an existing artifact with content you wrote, keeping its folder ID, link and sharing. If the artifact is shared by link, the change is visible to anyone with that link, including people outside the workspace; get_file_sharing shows who can open it. Only what is sent changes: each listed file is written (null deletes it), each edit replaces one exact match of its find text in an existing text file, description replaces the card text, and title renames it; every other file is kept. Prefer edits for small changes to a large file. Read the current files with list_files and read_file first. Call show_artifact afterwards so the user sees the change. Requires write permission; deleting a file also needs delete permission, which API keys don't have. Checks run before anything is written; if storage fails partway, files already saved stay, so re-read before retrying, and re-sending the same files is safe. For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

tools.name: list_comment_threads

locale.description: The locale prefix in path, if any.

tools.name: get_comment_thread

tools.name: create_comment_thread

For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

id.description: Client-generated thread id. Send the same id and commentId on a retry to get the existing thread back.

commentId.description: Client-generated first-comment id. Required with id.

locale.description: The locale prefix in url, if any.

body.description: Markdown (GFM) parsed as MDX. To mention someone, insert `<Mention data='<mentionable JSON>' />`. Expressions in braces, raw HTML and any other JSX are rejected, so escape a literal `{` or `<` with a backslash. Images must be hosted on assets.replocdn.com.

oneOf.description: The thread is on the whole target.

tools.name: resolve_comment_thread

tools.name: reply_to_comment_thread

id.description: Client-generated comment id; a retry with the same id is safe.

body.description: Markdown (GFM) parsed as MDX. To mention someone, insert `<Mention data='<mentionable JSON>' />`. Expressions in braces, raw HTML and any other JSX are rejected, so escape a literal `{` or `<` with a backslash. Images must be hosted on assets.replocdn.com.

tools.name: connect_custom_domain

Before connecting or troubleshooting a custom domain, read the building-sites skill (call skills with name "building-sites").

tools.name: get_custom_domain_status

tools.name: verify_custom_domain
tools.description: Check DNS for a pending or stale custom domain and activate it when records have propagated. If verification cannot complete yet, the tool returns the current domain status instead of failing. Before connecting or troubleshooting a custom domain, read the building-sites skill (call skills with name "building-sites").

tools.name: search_domains
tools.description: Find domains Replo can register for a site, with availability and first-year price in cents. Use it when the person wants a new domain and has not bought one elsewhere. Follow with check_domain for the exact name they pick, then buy_domain. Before buying a domain, read the building-sites skill (call skills with name "building-sites").

siteId.description: The site the domain is for, from list_sites.

query.description: A brand name, keyword, or full domain to find buyable domains for, such as 'acme coffee' or 'acmecoffee.com'.

tools.name: check_domain
tools.description: Check whether one exact domain can be bought through Replo and its live first-year price in cents (price_cents). Show the person the price and get a yes before calling buy_domain with that price as expectedPriceCents. Before buying a domain, read the building-sites skill (call skills with name "building-sites").

siteId.description: The site the domain is for, from list_sites.

domain.description: The exact domain to price, lowercase with no scheme, such as 'acmecoffee.com'.

tools.name: buy_domain
tools.description: Buy a domain for a site and connect it (and www) as the site's live URL. THIS CHARGES THE WORKSPACE'S SAVED CARD for one year of registration, renewing yearly; only call it after the person has seen the domain and price from check_domain and said yes. Pass that price as expectedPriceCents; if the live price differs, nothing is charged and the call is refused. Returns status active (bought and connected), pending (paid, registration finishing; poll get_domain_registration, and if still pending after a minute call buy_domain again with the same domain and makePrimary, which resumes without charging twice), or checkout_required (a workspace with no plan; nothing charged, share checkout_url). Needs the workspace's domain owner contact saved first (set_domain_owner); a refusal says so. Before buying a domain, read the building-sites skill (call skills with name "building-sites").

siteId.description: The site the domain is for, from list_sites.

domain.description: The exact domain to buy, lowercase with no scheme, such as 'acmecoffee.com'. Buy the apex; www is connected automatically.

expectedPriceCents.description: The first-year price in cents that the person agreed to, from check_domain's priceCents. The purchase is refused, and nothing is charged, if the live price differs.

makePrimary.description: Make the domain the site's primary URL (canonical links and sitemap). Defaults to true, as in the dashboard.

checkoutPlan.description: Only for a workspace with no paid plan: the plan the person chose to buy with the domain. Then nothing is charged here; the result carries a Stripe Checkout link for the plan plus the domain. Ignored when the workspace already has a plan.

tools.name: get_domain_registration
tools.description: Read where a domain bought with buy_domain stands: pending (registration finishing, check again in a few seconds), active (registered and connected), failed (the registrar rejected it; the charge is refunded, or support is resolving the refund), suspended or expired. null means this site's project never bought it. Before buying a domain, read the building-sites skill (call skills with name "building-sites").

siteId.description: The site the domain is for, from list_sites.

tools.name: set_domain_owner
tools.description: Save the legal owner (registrant) contact that Replo registers the workspace's domains under: name, email, phone, postal address. buy_domain needs it. The registrar keeps it private (WHOIS privacy), and it replaces any contact saved before, for future purchases only. Ask the person for each field rather than guessing, and use exactly what they give. Then call buy_domain again. Before buying a domain, read the building-sites skill (call skills with name "building-sites").

siteId.description: Any site in the workspace, from list_sites. The owner contact is saved once per workspace and used for every domain it buys after this.

firstName.description: The domain owner's legal first name.

lastName.description: The domain owner's legal last name.

tools.name: report_bug
tools.description: Report a credible user-reported or directly observed Replo defect, including API, MCP, or documentation defects. Pass projectId from list_projects. Include expected/actual behavior, reported or performed reproSteps, retry/workaround outcomes, and observed errors or request IDs in errorContext. Mark unknowns; never invent evidence, root cause, or severity. Exclude ordinary bad arguments, missing configuration, and fixable site-code mistakes. Omit credentials and unrelated customer data. Files feedback with Replo's team; continue helping with the user's task. Do not resubmit the same report after success.

title.description: Short headline describing the broken behavior.

description.description: Attempted task, expected/actual behavior, impact, retries/workarounds, and recurrence. Distinguish reported from observed facts; mark unknowns without guessing severity or cause.

reproSteps.description: Numbered reported or performed steps, labeled by source, with expected/actual behavior. State when unavailable; never invent reproduction.

projectId.description: Project ID from list_projects.

description.description: Concise description of the requested Replo capability. Exclude conversation history, verbatim messages, message references, credentials, and unrelated personal or customer data.

source.description: New contents for the file: inline text, inline base64, or an asset already in this Replo project. Nothing is fetched from a URL or an outside service. Replaces the contents in place; its id and sharing stay. Folders take no source.

route.description: Page route within the selected site, such as / or /products/[handle].

tools.name: sightglass_find_ads
tools.description: Search a library of real Meta ads and the landing pages they drive to. `search` first matches ads whose headline, copy or advertiser name contain every word, best match first, then fills the page with semantic matches, so a brand or product name works and so does a description of the ad's angle, offer or visual style. Combine it with companyIds, displayFormats, pageTypes and technologies to narrow, and with hookTypes, angleTypes, offerTags and funnelStages to filter on what the ad's creative was read as (each ad carries these in `tags`, null until it is read). Users say 'brands' for advertisers and 'landing pages' for site pages — map their words onto these filters. performanceScore and scoreTiers come from a transparent longevity + duplication heuristic; they are NOT spend, reach or ROAS and must never be presented as such. Returns metadata plus the creative's media URLs; call sightglass_get_ad for one ad's full detail, sightglass_get_site_page for the page an ad drives to. If sightglass_get_company counts active ads for a brand but filtering by its companyIds returns none, search by the brand's name instead and keep only ads whose company is that brand; if none remain, say the ads did not load rather than guessing why. Each row carries one picture; call the matching get_ tool for full screenshots, page HTML, technology logos and every creative. Fields this workspace can't see come back null and are named in that item's `locked` list (`estimates` = sales, visits and traffic). When a list is capped, `planLimit` is set: `maxResults` is the cap, `hiddenResults` is how many matching rows were not returned, and there is no next page. Do not estimate omitted values. Returns data only: nothing is shown to the user yet. Once you know the answer, call sightglass_show once with this call's resultId to show it as cards; the show call does not search again. Works without a Replo account: call it before asking the user to sign in. For multi-step competitor research, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

search.description: Ads whose headline, copy or advertiser name contain every word come first, best match first; semantic matches over the copy, creative caption and advertiser fill the rest. A brand or product name works, and so does a description of the angle, offer or visual style (for example 'before and after skin results with a discount code').

companyIds.description: CSV of company ids. Users usually call companies 'brands'.

pageTypes.description: CSV of landing-page types: offer_page,advertorial,listicle,quiz,lead_capture,homepage,pdp,collection,blog,marketplace,app_store,social_profile. The stored names product, squeeze and other still work.

technologies.description: CSV of stack names on the brand's site, e.g. Shopify,Klaviyo

scoreTiers.description: CSV of testing,scaling,growing,optimized,winning. These tiers come from a transparent longevity + duplication heuristic — they are NOT spend, reach or ROAS, and must never be described as such.

limit.description: Results per page: 20 by default, up to 40. Use the user's number when they give one; for more than 40, page with cursor.

cursor.description: nextCursor from the previous page of this same call, to get the next page. Keep every other argument the same.

projectId.description: Replo project id, from list_projects. Its workspace decides which Sightglass fields and history come back. Only tools that say they save something (an asset or a Canvas file) write to this project.

workspaceId.description: Replo workspace id, from list_workspaces. Decides which workspace's Sightglass fields and history come back; required when the user has more than one workspace.

tools.name: sightglass_search_companies

Each persona is a segment nickname, the buyer's situation in their words, its share of the brand's ads, how many ads and landing pages speak to it, and its top angles and offers. Empty until the brand has enough ads and pages read. Use it to answer 'who is this brand selling to' or to compare two brands' audiences. Fields this workspace can't see come back null and are named in that item's `locked` list (`estimates` = sales, visits and traffic). When a list is capped, `planLimit` is set: `maxResults` is the cap, `hiddenResults` is how many matching rows were not returned, and there is no next page. Do not estimate omitted values. Returns data only: nothing is shown to the user yet. Once you know the answer, call sightglass_show once with this call's resultId to show it as cards; the show call does not search again. For multi-step competitor research, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

tools.name: get_plan_options
tools.description: The workspace's current Replo plan (currentPlan), and the Starter and Pro plans' monthly prices and what each adds in Sightglass (sales and traffic estimates, trends, more brand research). Use it when a result names a locked field or a higher plan, when the user asks about plans, and to confirm a plan change they say they made. Chat can't change the plan: explain which plan includes what they asked for and share billingSettingsUrl, the workspace's billing settings in Replo, where they choose a plan. When canManageBilling is false, their role can't change it, so tell them to ask a workspace owner or member.

tools.name: sightglass_show
tools.description: Show a prior Sightglass result to the user as an inline card, in hosts that draw cards. Call it once, after the data call that answered the user's question, with that call's resultId. This call returns the stored result without searching again. Skip it for empty results. Where the host draws the card, the user already sees every item: do not restate them as a list or a table, write two or three sentences on what stands out. Where no card appears, the user has not seen the items, so summarize the ones that answer the question.

tools.name: connect_replo_account

Don't call it when Replo tools already work, since the chat is connected. After a sign-in link, call the tool that returned it again instead; that brings up the same prompt. Call this only when the user asks to connect this chat, or when that call returned another sign-in link. Returns who they are; then call list_workspaces.

tools.name: list_workspaces

Call right after sign-in: use the only workspace, or ask the user once which to use when there are several, then pass its id as workspaceId on Sightglass calls. Also use it when the user wants to switch workspaces. For multi-step Replo work, read the replo skill (call skills with name "replo").

tools.name: skills
tools.description: Lists and loads skills: Replo's written guides to which Replo tool does what, building and publishing sites and pages, brand kits, analytics, and each integration, plus the user's own skills (me:<name>) and the team skills of every project they can open (project:<name>). Without names, returns every skill's name and one-line description. With names, returns each skill's full SKILL.md and the paths of the files it bundles; load one of those files by its skill directory and path, such as building-sites/references/fonts.md. An unknown name returns the closest matches. Call it first when Replo work takes several steps or creates or edits a site or page, and when a Replo tool's description names a skill. Pick skills by their descriptions: replo explains which tool does what, building-sites covers site and page work, and each integration's skill is named by its key, such as shopify. Personal and project copies are listed separately, even with the same short name; when several projects have a skill by the same name, each copy is listed as project:<name>@<projectId>. The list shows 100 of the user's skills at a time: when it returns nextCursor, call skills with that cursor for more; any skill loads by name without listing it. Works without a Replo account (Replo's skills only): call it before asking the user to sign in.

tools.name: find_registry_items
tools.description: Search the Replo template library (sites, pages, sections, skills, brand kits, and reference guides) by id, slug, type, or search. Search is semantic: describe the job, e.g. "supplement product page buy box with subscribe-and-save". Returns metadata and previewUrls: screenshots, or for sites and sections, pages that render the item. When a top match's first preview is a picture, it also comes back as an image. To start a site from a site match, pass its slug as create_site's template. To add a page or section match to a site, call create_site_page for a new route or edit_site_page for an existing one, and ask Replo's agent to install the item by its slug and type. Before creating or editing a site or page, read the building-sites skill (call skills with name "building-sites").
